summary: Backend tested comprehensively (24 tests across 10 modules). 23/24 passed (95.8%). All auth, subscription (mocked Razorpay), trading buy/sell flow, portfolio, orders, analytics, watchlist, leaderboard, what-if, autopsy, stock market data and search work correctly. One failing test (crypto quote for BTC) is a transient external rate-limit from CoinGecko free API returning 429 -> backend wraps as 502. Stock data via yfinance worked reliably with retry.

minor.issue: Intermittently returns 502 'Crypto provider error' when CoinGecko free API is rate-limited (HTTP 429). Confirmed via direct curl to coingecko: 429 'Rate Limit'. Suggestion: extend _QUOTE_TTL for crypto (e.g. 60-120s), retry with backoff, or fall back to cached/last-known price. Currently market/overview happened to be cached so it passed; subsequent fresh quote fails. Same risk exists for /api/market/history (crypto) and /api/whatif (crypto).

action_items: Improve CoinGecko resilience: increase crypto cache TTL (e.g., 60-120s), add 1-retry with backoff on 429/5xx in _cg_quote and history endpoints, and on rate-limit fall back to last cached price instead of raising 502.
Consider returning 429 (not 502) when upstream rate-limits so clients can implement proper retry-after handling.
Optional: Use POST /api/watchlist returns generic {ok: true} even for duplicates (silently swallowed). Consider returning 409 on duplicate for clarity (low priority).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is ~800 lines and contains everything (models, auth, market, trading, watchlist, leaderboard, whatif, autopsy, subscription, curated list). Consider splitting into modules (routers/auth.py, routers/market.py, routers/trade.py, services/market_data.py).

get_quote is called synchronously inside async endpoints (e.g., /api/portfolio loops through holdings calling yfinance/requests). This blocks the event loop and can be slow with many holdings. Consider running in thread executor (asyncio.to_thread) or batching.
_QUOTE_CACHE TTL of 15s is too aggressive for crypto with rate-limited free API; raise per-provider TTLs.
JWT_SECRET falls back to a hardcoded dev secret in code; in production this should fail-fast if missing.
_cg_quote: when 24h change is 0 or missing, prev = price so change = 0. Acceptable, but be aware change_pct returns the raw upstream value without sanity bounds.
load_dotenv ordering looks correct (loaded before os.environ reads). Good.
seed_data_creation: Tests create fresh users per session with prefix 'titan_test_' and 'poor_'. No cleanup performed; new user per pytest run. MongoDB will accumulate test users; main agent may want a cleanup job.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend public URL: https://paper-market-hub.preview.emergentagent.com (EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL). All routes /api/*. Test suite at /app/backend/tests/test_trading_titans.py uses a single registered session-scoped user for auth flows and creates a 'poor' user for insufficient-balance test. CoinGecko free tier rate-limits aggressively; expect intermittent 502 on /api/market/quote?market=crypto and /api/market/history (crypto). Stock endpoints via yfinance worked reliably with one retry. Razorpay subscription is MOCKED — POST /api/subscription/activate directly credits ₹100,000 without payment verification.
rca_of_issue: Crypto quote 502 RCA: CoinGecko free-tier rate limit. Direct curl to https://api.coingecko.com/api/v3/simple/price returned HTTP 429 with 'You've exceeded the Rate Limit'. Backend _cg_quote raises HTTPException(502, 'Crypto provider error') for any non-200 response. Reproduction: hit /api/market/quote?symbol=BTC&market=crypto repeatedly within a minute on free CoinGecko. Mitigation: increase per-provider cache TTL, retry with backoff, fall back to last known price. Not a functional code bug — upstream constraint.
mocked_apis_verified: Razorpay: /api/subscription/create-order returns mock order id, /api/subscription/activate directly credits ₹100,000 to wallet and sets subscription_active=true without signature verification — VERIFIED working as designed. Second activation correctly returns 400.
